findings.title: Protective appearance without truth claim
findings.claim: The sleepers' apparent wakefulness can also function as a protective misdirection: it changes an observer's estimate and turns intrusion away without making the estimate true.
findings.mechanism: The focus verb carries the supposition branch through 18:18:1:2; the supplied 2:273, 24:39, and 18:104 appearance-versus-reality connections return that carrier, so a visible posture can deter access while remaining a false assessment.
findings.reader_payoff: The scene becomes a bounded test of how an appearance can protect a hidden state while perception remains mistaken.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains that the sleepers are asleep and only appear awake. The protective function is a contextual resonance, not a truth claim about the appearance, a moral equivalence with 18:104, or a general theory of deception.

epistemic.reason: The trusted focus publication supplies the bounded protective relation, while the legacy reader walk and exact wider connections support its contextual extension.

findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains living people asleep in the cave. The wider sleep-and-return parallels do not equate the sleepers with the dead, assert resurrection as the local event, or fix one theory of the interval.
